as_told: Alfred Nobel left mathematics out of his prizes because his wife had an affair with a mathematician. The mathematician is often named as Gösta Mittag-Leffler, the leading Swedish mathematician of the time. Nobel, the story goes, did not want his rival to win a prize.
lesson: Great institutions are often shaped by petty personal grudges.
what_happened: Nobel had no wife. His will of 27 November 1895 leaves money to nephews, nieces, friends and servants and names no wife of his. In a letter to his brother Ludvig he listed as one of his 'principal faults' that 'he has no family'. The will sets up five prizes (physics, chemistry, physiology or medicine, literature and peace) and gives no reason for leaving out mathematics. The earliest telling of the wife version I found is a joke in a 1961 joke book, whose punchline is that Nobel was a bachelor. A milder version, that Nobel wanted to keep Mittag-Leffler from winning, appears in Howard Eves's 1969 'In Mathematical Circles'; I could not read that book in full.
false_part: Nobel had no wife, so no wife of his had an affair with a mathematician.

earliest_telling.where: Hanukkah Latkes and Rothschild's Millions: A Collection of Jewish Wit and Humor (New York: Twayne Publishers), page 218 of the scan
earliest_telling.quote: affections of Nobel’s wife and, for spite, he

original.what: Nobel's own letter to his brother Ludvig, who had asked him for biographical notes, as printed in the authorised biography by Henrik Schück and Ragnar Sohlman (Sohlman was an executor of the will)
original.date: printed 1929; the letter is undated, and Ludvig Nobel died in 1888, so it was written before then
original.quote: virtues : keeping his nails clean and never being a burden to any

original.what: The same letter, the line about family
original.quote: one. Principal faults: that he has no family, is bad tempered

original.what: Nobel's will of 27 November 1895 (English translation published by the Nobel Foundation); it lists the heirs (nephews, nieces, friends, servants) with no wife, then names five prize fields and gives no reason for the choice
original.quote: My nephews, Hjalmar and Ludvig Nobel, sons of my brother Robert Nobel

original.what: The punchline of the 1961 joke itself, which says Nobel was a bachelor

lesson_verdict.why: I found no study on how often personal grudges shape the design of institutions. The will, the one record of Nobel's choice, gives no motive at all, so this case cannot support the lesson either way.

source.what: Nobel's will, cited only to show that it states no reason for the five fields; it is not evidence for the general lesson
source.quote: The interest is to be divided into five equal parts and distributed as follows

search_steps: Open Library full-text search '"nobel" "mittag-leffler" "wife" "mathematics"' (1,059 hits; looked at the first 50): earliest relevant hits were 1984 Cooke (cites a 1966 Mathematics Teacher note 'Mathematics and the Nobel Prize') and 1987 Polya picture album (Mittag-Leffler version).

Open Library full-text search '"no nobel prize in mathematics"' (first 100 hits sorted by year): earliest was Howard Eves, In Mathematical Circles (1969), item 352°, a Mittag-Leffler version with no wife; the scan is lending-only, so I could not read it in full.

Open Library full-text search '"nobel's wife" mathematician' (first 100 hits): earliest was David Schwartz, Hanukkah Latkes and Rothschild's Millions (1961); later hits from 1989 to 2008 repeat the wife version. A 1989 journalism textbook cites a 1986 New York Times letter by T. Blomgren headed 'Nobel's wife' as a correction; I did not find that letter.

Two further Open Library queries ('"affections of Nobel's wife"', '"blackballed the whole" nobel mathematics') returned longer snippets of the 1961 joke, including the punchline that Nobel was a bachelor; saved both result files. The book itself is lending-only on archive.org, so the quotes come from search snippets.
Did not find the 1966 Mathematics Teacher note or the 1985 Garding and Hörmander note in Mathematical Intelligencer in free full text.
Original record: saved the Nobel Foundation's English text of the will from nobelprize.org.
Searched nobelprize.org pages for a statement that Nobel never married; the biography page has it only as a quiz option. Britannica's print page refused the download (403).

Found the 1929 English edition of Schück and Sohlman, The Life of Alfred Nobel, in full text on archive.org (TheLifeOfAlfredNobel); it prints Nobel's own letter saying he has no family. Another copy (in.ernet.dli.2015.176373) had no text file (404).
Looked for a study on grudges and institutions; found none.
confidence_note: The 1961 quotes come from Open Library search snippets, not from a full text, because the book is lending-only. I may have missed earlier tellings in newspapers; I did not search newspaper archives for this story. The records I quote for Nobel having no wife are his own letter, written before 1888, saying he had no family, and his 1895 will, which names no wife among its heirs. Ludvig Nobel's death in 1888 is stated in the same 1929 biography.
